label: copy phase: input y when the next output is d (the original y->d bigram), late in recall
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the input is y (94% of activation mass; input d has the remaining 6%). It is strongest when the output at that step is d, meaning the original sequence had the bigram y d (82% of mass has out_tok d). It is essentially silent for recall_idx below 3, and at t < 8. Strongest examples have y d in the middle of the original, e.g. d 3 c k y d ... recalled at position 4. Many y->d copy steps stay inactive, mostly at the last outputs of short sequences, so precision is only about 0.6. There are also weak activations on copy-phase y inputs with other outputs (y, c, others). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on the first occurrence of a token.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=y (+5.94), in_tok=y (+3.96), phase=2 & out_tok=d (+3.75), out_tok=d (+3.58), phase=2 & in_tok=d (+3.32), in_tok=d (+2.69). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.12), recall_idx=1 (-2.41), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.41), prev2_tok=<DEL> (-2.24).
